narration.text: Searchbloom publishes this agency list and ranks itself first, so its ranking reflects the publisher's own assessment, not an independent verdict.
Throughout this guide, the source is Searchbloom: its facts come from company websites, and its case-study figures are the companies' own reporting.

scenes.visual_direction: Place the self-ranking disclosure and case-study sourcing in two stacked cards, bringing each forward as its narration is heard.

narration.text: Start by defining success: leads, sign-ups, or revenue from AI referrals, rather than citation counts or visibility scores.
Then ask for a dated AI search result with a named or described company, a figure, and a period.
Watch for promises of AI citations in weeks, or reports that count citations without mentioning leads or revenue.

on_screen.text: Searchbloom recommends tracking leads from AI referrals

scenes.visual_direction: Center the outcome takeaway beside an abstract evidence card; reveal empty date, company, figure, and period compartments without adding example results.

narration.text: AI answers are probabilistic: repeating the same question can produce different brands.
Track a fixed set of real buyer questions daily across the AI platforms your buyers use, then read the trend.
Separate branded and non-branded prompts, and segment them by awareness, consideration, and purchase.
Ask which tracking tool, prompts, platforms, and run frequency an agency uses.

scenes.visual_direction: Animate one question card returning different abstract answer arrangements, then organize repeated question cards into a calendar grid without numerical results or trend lines.

narration.text: In Searchbloom's own tracking, about nine of every ten sources AI cites are on other people's sites.
Ask which outside URLs are retrieved and cited for your top buyer questions, and which placements the agency can help you secure.
When an answer leaves your business out, inspect the pages it cited; often, the fix is a listing through outreach, a review, or sponsorship.

scenes.visual_direction: Arrange an abstract answer panel beside outside-page cards; draw connectors from the answer to those cards, then highlight one card as the inspection step is discussed.

narration.text: Crawler access, correct structured data, and clean architecture make a site legible to AI platforms.
The agency should handle technical, content, and entity work, and review visibility tracking with you monthly.
Clarify whether the agency implements technical changes or supplies technical recommendations, and price the developer time you will need to provide.

scenes.visual_direction: Arrange a site schematic showing technical work above two lanes for implementation and recommendations; reveal a developer task card in each lane as the narration explains delivery responsibilities.

narration.text: Your team must own sponsorship and affiliate budgets when the most-retrieved roundup in your category is a paid placement.
Your team must also own retailer, marketplace, and partner listings.
That responsibility extends to social media and community work, brand positioning, and the budget behind PR.

scenes.visual_direction: Place a client-team silhouette at the center and connect abstract budget, listing, and community cards around it; emphasize the budget card during the closing sentence.

narration.text: In Searchbloom's comparison of nine companies, three publish a fee, two a minimum, and four a contract term.
Before comparing agencies, get any unpublished fees, minimums, and contract lengths in writing.

on_screen.text: To get unpublished terms in writing

scenes.visual_direction: Arrange three document compartments for fee, minimum, and contract information, using only abstract marks; consolidate them into one written-terms document as the final takeaway appears.
